description: §42.4 statement 10: the arms of a ternary that is the condition's value (or an operand of its `!` / `&&` / `||`) are inside the condition — an unresolved arm or arm operand is E-COND-NOT-BOOLEAN, once per site.
rationale: §42.4 statement 10: "A ternary that IS the condition's value, or an operand in its `!` / `&&` / `||` chain, is inside the condition: each arm is that value when taken … `if (@b ? !g() : @c)`, `if (@b ? (g() && @c) : @c)`, `if (@b ? g() : @c)` and `if ((@b ? g() : @c) && @c)` each report `g()`". Provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S460 "a on F2, go" (PA reading: ternary arms of the condition's value are inside the condition). S478 (bootstrap triage F1): `g` now returns a value typed `asIs`, one of statement 5's own unresolved sources ("a value typed `asIs` / `unknown` (§7.5.2)"; the §42.4 worked example's `u: asIs`), so `g()`'s return type is neither declared nor inferred. The earlier `function g() { }` no longer tests this: "a call of a function that returns nothing is not a value (§48 \"The return rule\", rule 3; E-TYPE-001 in a value position)" (§4.14; S469 "fall-off and tail returns: ALWAYS EXPLICIT"), so `g()` is E-TYPE-001 inside the condition, and §42.4 statement 6 ("No second report": no statement-5 report "when the compiler has already reported any Error-severity diagnostic whose span lies within the condition") then rightly suppresses E-COND-NOT-BOOLEAN.
